samples.summary: SMA shell exploit: scope SSRF and bind rollback traversal
SMA curl exploit: --data implies POST; bind rollback traversal
SMA Python exploit: detect local-service SSRF and rollback traversal

identity: Minimal SonicWall SMA1000 exploit-attempt clients; no malware-family identity established
limitations: No payload upload, Erlang distribution handshake, command dispatch, persistence or exfiltration is present.
Scripts assume an existing privileged session and staged shell file.
Shell websocat invocation blocks until session closes; its missing Connect Agent header may prevent the documented bypass.
Python opens a connection but sends no WebSocket frames; POST is a separate authenticated AMC request.
Percent encoding is normal HTTP form encoding, not code obfuscation.
corrections: Moved all neutral original atoms and neutral query/local-target composites from the exploit leaf into existing capability leaves.
Rollback attack now requires traversal specifically in hotfix=, rather than any temp traversal in the file.
Negative bookmark prefix plus local target required for tunnel abuse.
Erlang service SSRF requires port 1050; no longer labels port 8188 as Erlang.
Cookie/node co-occurrence described as references, not proven handshake or RCE.
Root rollback execution attempt belongs in privilege-escalation appliance exploit leaf.
placement_review: Pass 1: independently classified each matcher by required evidence (protocol, interface, location, or abuse).
Pass 2: reviewed nearest alternatives: proxy target versus C2; RPC versus OS service; application state versus configuration; privilege escalation versus generic execution.
consumer_audit: rg found no external exact consumers of migrated SMA IDs or broad selectors for the original SMA leaf. Proxy target ancestor consumers select named unrelated relay traits; new atoms do not widen them. Exact Python consumers follow renamed traits; requests ancestor any-selectors retain explicit moved POST and import alternatives; redundant POST legs covered by POST selectors removed. Constructed URL observations retain their original homes.

controls.renamed-payload.sh: 2 hostile traits despite renamed staged script/bookmark suffix

migration.sma-wsproxy-loopback-tunnel: retained; negative bookmark bypass pattern required
migration.sma-wsproxy-erlang-service-ssrf: retained; require negative bookmark, local target, and port 1050

coverage_changes: Port 1050 now bound to wsproxy query target, including IPv6 and mapped IPv4 destinations. Old unbound localhost:1050 string is insufficient alone.

Connect Agent value is a parser literal so Python dict headers match as well as shell raw headers when string value is separate; complete raw header strings are still reported by general HTTP header rules.
Neutral fields no longer inherit exploit ATT&CK mappings or assessment-plugin exclusions. Hostile consumers keep the assessment-plugin exclusion.
Original generic path and node references remain neutral observations; their wording asserts neither access nor appliance identity.
python_matcher_changes: Arbitrary .post() calls no longer imply HTTP. Consumers use canonical structured HTTP-client POST calls; canonical receiver family now includes aiohttp.
Requests/websocket imports use engine import facts; exact consumers updated.
Native POST request-line duplicate consolidated with canonical post-request-line; valid request-line shape now required and C/C++/Go source scope retained.
fixture_correction: Legacy-tag probe only prints bookmark protocol fields; moved hostile fixture to benign, required neutral migrated traits and forbade objectives.
